3.  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote Teleconference/Virtual City Council Meetings
  Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361
  At the November 16, 2021 City Council meeting, the City Council made findings pursuant
  to Assembly Bill 361 to continue to meet remotely. To continue this practice, it is required,
  that the City Council determine that the COVID-19 state of emergency proclaimed by the
  Governor still exists and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue
  to have teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or
  recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19. and
  that as a result of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent
  risks to the health or safety of attendees, Because these findings must be made every
  thirty (30) days. the City Council will have to make these findings at its upcoming May 3,
  2022 meeting and thirty (30) days thereafter.
  Recommended Action
  Determine that the COVID-1 9 state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists
  and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue to have
  teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
  measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result
  of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the
  health or safety of attendees.

4.  Adopt an Ordinance Amendment ZOA 22-Cl, which Amends the Avalon Municipal Code
  to Regulate SB 9 Urban Lot Splits and Two-Unit Proiects and Finds the Ordinance to be
  Exempt from CEQA
  This ordinance was introduced and all further readings waived at the March 1, 2022
  regular City Council meeting. Senate Bill 9 (SB 9) took effect on January 1, 2022 and
  requires the City to both: (1) allow any lot in a single-family residential zone to be split,
  roughly into halves, with resulting lots as small as 1,200 stand (2) allow any lot in a
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
APRIL 5, 2022
PAGE 3

  single-family residential zone to be developed with up to two single4amily primary
  dwellings. SB 9 supplants local zoning ordinances and only allows cities to impose
  certain objective criteria for projects covered by SB 9. The proposed Zoning Ordinance
  incorporates the state mandated changes but also creates certain objective standards
  by which such projects may be considered.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt an ordinance of the City of Avalon amending the Avalon Municipal Code to add
  Section 9-2.10 and Article 7 to Chapter 9-5 regarding SB 9 urban lot splits and two- unit
  projects.

GENERAL BUSINESS

5.  Website Redesign
  At the direction of City Council, City Staff began the process to update the City of Avaon
  website. By better utilizing technology, specifically, the City’s website, City Staff hope to
  streamline processes, and provide better overall customer service and accessibility.
  Recommended Action
  Consider proposals to update and redesign the City of Avalon website. Authorize Staff
  to enter into an agreement with CivicPlus for a year one contract amount not to exceed
  $50,000.

6.  Approval of Encroachment Permit for frontage improvements at 209 Beacon Street
  The applicant in conjunction with neighboring property owner at 215 Beacon, is
  requesting approval of a Site Plan (companion application) to allow the remodel of an
  existing portion of publicly owned property fronting 209 Beacon Street in the High Density
  Residential zone, The scope of work includes alterations to accessory/landscaping
  structures currently located within the City right of way, which will also require approval
  of an Encroachment from City Council.
  Recommended Action
  Approve encroachment permit for frontage improvements at 209 Beacon and authorize
  City Staff to negotiate with the property owners to determine the amounts of the
  required bond and lability insurance.
7.  Approval of Encroachment Permit for frontage improvements at 215 Beacon Street
  The applicant! in conjunction with neighboring property owner at 209 Beacon. is
  requesting approval of a Site Plan (companion application) to allow the remodel of an
  existing portion of publicly owned property fronting 215 Beacon Street in the High Density
  Residential zone. The scope of work includes alterations to accessory/landscaping
  structures currently located within the City right of way, which will also require approval
  of an Encroachment from City Council.
  Recommended Action
  Approve encroachment permit for frontage improvements at 215 Beacon and authorize
  City Staff to negotiate with the property owners to determine the amounts of the required
  bond and liability insurance.

Due to health recommendations from the Center for Disease Control and State of California
Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), and the declared state of emergency
wherein social distancing measures have been imposed or recommended, the CITY OF
AVALON’S CITY COUNCIL and PLANNING COMMISSION MEETINGS SHALL GENERALLY
BE AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC REMOTELY. The general public may attend the meetin9 in
the Council Chambers however must adhere to social distancing requirements and wear a mask
or face covering at all times. The public is encouraged to watch and participate from the safety
of their homes while practicing social distancing.

Council Chambers are open to a maximum 30 members of the general public. Once the Council
Chambers reach maximum occupancy, the general public may participate in Oral
Communication and address the City Council on an agenda item in person by waiting in the City
Hall Court Yard and entering the Chambers one at a time at the appropriate time. No one will be
admitted into the Council Chambers who is ill or exhibiting symptoms of COVID-19. All
individuals entering the Council Chambers must wear a mask or face covering at all times.
Additionally, the general public may participate in Oral Communication and address the City
Council on an agenda items by providing comments via e-Comment. Please use the link below
to provide comments via e-Comment.

  Approving an Encroachment Permit to Allow a Privately Maintained Parking Pad
  and Frontage Improvements within the Public Right-of-Way at 201 East Whittley;
  APN 7480-027-004.

  Approved encroachment permit for frontage improvements at 201 E. Whittley and
  authorized City Staff to negotiate with the property owners to determine the
  amounts of the required bond and liability insurance.
  Motion to approve made by Cinde Cassidy, seconded by Michael Ponce.
  (All Ayes)

11.  Outdoor Dining Program Revisited
  Authorized implementation of an outdoor dining program with the addition of the
  space around Wrigley Stage as a dinning location until June 20, 2024, or, unless
  earlier rescinded by the City Council or City Manager. Outdoor dining is
  prohibited on special event days.
  Motion to approve made by Cinde Cassidy, seconded by Michael Ponce.
  (All Ayes)

SUBJECT:  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote Teleconference/Virtual City
  Council Meetings Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Determine that the COVID-19 state of emergency proclaimed
by the Governor still exists and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue
to have teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result of the
COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health or safety
of attendees.

REPORT SUMMARY: Traditionally, the Brown Act allows for teleconference or virtual meetings,
provided that the physical locations of the legislative body’s members joining by teleconference
are posted on the agenda, that those locations are open to the public and that a quorum of the
members is located within its jurisdiction. Newly enacted AB 361 provides an exception to these
procedures in order to allow for fully virtual meetings during proclaimed emergencies, including
the COVID-19 pandemic.

Since March of 2020 and the issuance of Governor Newsom’s Executive Order N-29-20, which
suspended portions of the Brown Act relating to teleconferencing, the City Council has had virtual
meetings without having to post the location of the legislative body members attending virtually.
Most public agencies have been holding public meetings using virtual platforms since this time.
In June of 2021, Governor Newsom issued Executive Order N-08-21, which provided that the
exceptions contained in EO N-29-20 would sunset on September 30, 2021.

On September 10, 2021, the Legislature adopted AS 361, which allows public agencies to hold
fully virtual meetings under certain circumstances without the posting of the agenda from each
location a legislative body member is attending. Governor Newsom signed the bill into law on
September 16, 2021. Because it contained an urgency provision, it took immediate effect.

Specific Findings Required under AS 361

Under AB 361, the City Council can hold virtual meetings without providing notice of the City
Council’s teleconference location if the City Council makes the determination that there is a
Governor-proclaimed state of emergency, which the City Council will consider in their
determination, and one of two secondary criteria listed below exists:

  1. State or local officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social
  distancing in connection with COVID-19; or

   2. The City CouncU determines that requiring a meeting in person would present an
  imminent risk to the health or safety of attendees.

COVID-19 continues to present an imminent threat to the health or safety of members of the
public: and the Governor’s declaration of a CDVI D-19 emergency still exists. Although vaccines
are now widely available, many people in the State and County are still not fully vaccinated and
remain susceptible to infection. The disease can still spread rapidly through person-to-person
contact and those in close proximity. Further, more contagious variants of the disease are now
present in the State and County, the most predominant of which is a new variant of the Omnicron
variant. The City’s economy is dependent upon visitors to the island: the presence of which.
increases the likelihood of transmission of the disease. Also, having members of the public attend
council meetings at locations where council members are in attendance due to their desire to
avoid exposure to CDVID-19 poses an imminent risk to the health or safety of attendees.

Re-Authorization is Required Within 30 Days

The City Council made the findings listed above at its March 15, 2022 City Council meeting.
Consistent with the provisions of Government Code Section 54953(e), the findings must be made
every 30 days after teleconferencing for the first time” under AB 361. Thus, if the City Council
desires to continue to meet remotely without having to post the location of each teleconference
location, the City Council must again find that the COVID-19 emergency still exists and that one
of the two following findings can be made: that state or local officials have imposed or
recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, or, that a
result of the COVID-1 9 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health
or safety of attendees. Because these findings must be made every thirty (30) days, the City
Council will have to make these findings at its upcoming May 3, 2022 meeting and thirty (30)
days thereafter.

It is recommended that the City Council make these findings.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City Council will
have to follow the Brown Act provisions that existed prior to the CDVI D-19 pandemic.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: That the City Council make the findings under AB 361 at its May 3. 2022
City Council meeting.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: N/A

FISCAL IMPACTS: None.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: This item was properly listed on the posted
agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

SUBJECT:  Adopt Zoning Ordinance Amendment ZOA 22-01, which Amends
  the Avalon Municipal Code to Regulate SB 9 Urban Lot Splits and
  Two-Unit Projects and Finds the Ordinance to be Exempt from
  CEQA

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adopt an ordinance of the City of Avalon amending the Avalon
Municipal Code to add Section 9-2.10 and Article 7 to Chapter 9-5 regarding SB 9 urban lot splits
and two- unit projects.

REPORT SUMMARY: This ordinance was introduced and all further readings waived at the
March 1, 2022 regular City Council meeting.

The California legislature recently passed, and Governor Newsom signed into law, Senate Bill
9 (‘SB 9”). SB 9 took effect on January 1, 2022 and requires the City to both: (1) allow any lot
in a single-family residential zone to be split, roughly into halves, with resulting lots as small as
1,200 sf and (2) allow any lot in a single-family residential zone to be developed with up to two
single-family primary dwellings. SB 9 requires the City to approve eligible lot splits and two-unit
projects ministerially (i.e., without discretionary review, conditions, or a hearing). Property
owners can also utilize both of SB 9’s provisions, meaning that an SB 9 lot split may be followed
with an SB 9 two-unit project on each of the two new lots, resulting in four total dwellings on
what was formerly one single-family residential lot  —  all with only ministerial approval.
  I

SB 9 supplants local zoning ordinances and only allows cities to impose certain objective criteria
for projects covered by SB 9. The proposed Zoning Ordinance incorporates the state mandated
changes but also creates certain objective standards by which such projects may be
considered. Most important to the City, applicants for such units will generally not have to
process their developments through the Planning Commission. The proposed Zoning
Ordinance Amendment ZOA 22-01 (attached as Attachment 1 and referred to herein as the
 ‘Ordinance”) implements SB 9 by adding Section 9-2.10 to the City’s Subdivision title (to
address urban lot splits), and Article 7 to Chapter 9-5 of the City’s Zoning title (to address two-
unit projects). The Ordinance will apply in the LD (Low Density Residential and Low Intensity
Recreational) zone.

 Background:

SB 9 allows cities to impose objective zoning, subdivision, and design standards (collectively
“objective development standards”) on covered lot splits and two-unit projects. An objective
standard is a regulation that does not involve personal or subjective judgment and that is
verifiable by reference to an external and uniform benchmark or criterion (e.g., a height limit).

Generally, the proposed Ordinance is written to allow the City to exercise as much local control
over SB 9 projects as state law allows. Among other things, the Ordinance includes regulations
governing the following:

  •  Location (LD [Low Density Residential and Low Intensity Recreational] zones; not in
  sensitive, dangerous, historic areas; not on rental property (within last 3 years))
  •  Lot Size (2,400 sf mm to split; 1,200 sf mm for resulting)
  •  Lot Access (adjoin ROW)
  •  Unit Size (800 sf max! du)
  •  Setbacks (normal, except as necessary to allow two units at 800 sf each; but no less
  than 4 feet side and rear)
  •  Use (residential-only, no short-term rental)
  •  Parking (one space, unless exempt by statute)
  •  Owner occupancy (three-year minimum on urban splits; permanent on two-unit projects)
  •  Architecture (must match other dwelling or dwellings on property; no direct lines of sight)
  •  Landscaping (limits on tree removal; required screening)
  •  Utilities (direct connections to service providers; all underground)
  •  Separate Conveyance Within a Lot (prohibited; no condos, no timeshares or separate-
  use co-ownerships)
  •  Deed Restriction (required; no short-term rental, non-residential use, or separate
  conveyance; development limited to SB 9 projects)

As noted above, the proposed Ordinance retains as much local control as possible under these
new State imposed mandates. Examples include the following:

  •  SB 9 does not contain standards governing architecture, landscaping, or fire hazard
  mitigation measures. The Ordinance imposes City-specific architecture, landscaping,
  and fire hazard mitigation measures on SB 9 projects in the City. 1

  •  SB 9 does not specifically regulate height; any height limit must be imposed by the local
  agency. The Ordinance provides that new SB 9-mandated primary dwelling units are
  subject to the LD zone’s height restrictions (LD zones are the only areas where SB 9
  projects are allowed in the City). 2

  •  56 9 generally allows—but does not require—local agencies to impose their standard
  setback requirements on SB 9 projects. The Ordinance imposes the LD zone’s setback

Environmental Review:
Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (‘CEQA”) and the City’s local CEQA
Guidelines, staff has determined the project exempt from further environmental review pursuant
to: (1) Section 15358 of the CEQA Guidelines because it will not result in a direct or reasonably
foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment; (2) Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA
Guidelines as there is no possibility that this activity will have a significant adverse effect on the
environment; and (3) Government Code sections 65852.21(j) and 66411.7(n), which provide that
adoption of an ordinance implementing the provisions of Government Code sections 66411.7
and 65852.21 (i.e. SB 9) is statutorily exempt from CEQA.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Compliance with State regulations while maintaining as much local control
as possible.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Undetermined.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City would be
limited to applying the State mandates and the City’s existing objective development standards.
Approving such projects based solely on the States mandates and the City’s existing standards
would, among other things, threaten the character of existing neighborhoods and negatively
impact property values, personal privacy, and fire safety as many of the City standards would
be supplanted by the State’s mandates.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Publish a Summary of the Ordinance and implement City Council
decision.

SUBJECT:  Website Redesign

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Consider proposals to update and redesign the City of Avalon
website. Authorize Staff to enter into an agreement with CivicPlus for a year one contract amount
not to exceed $50,000.

REPORT SUMMARY: At the direction of City Council, City Staff began the process to update
the City of Avalon website.

City Staff compiled a wish list of features for a new site that included:
  -  Modernization of the overall site;
  -  Compliance with ADA Standards;
  -  Calendar feature;
  -  Ability to accept online payments;
  -  Ability to enhance public engagement via push notifications for text or email;
  -  More user4riendly interface for Staff attempting to modify the site without formal training;
  -  A form submission feature with automated workflows; and
  -  A more intuitive search capability.

Additionally, City Staff hoped to be able to consolidate vendors by finding one firm that could
provide the abovementioned services as well as supplant services currently provided by
Grannicus, eCode, Zoom, and/or RecPro.

Staff solicited proposals from five qualified firms specializing in the development of government
websites Town Web, Revize, QScend Technologies, Inc., CivicPlus and Freshie Sites. The
  —

City received proposals from Town Web, Revize, QScend Technologies, Inc., and CivicPlus.

City Staff attempted to create an apples-to-apples comparison of the potential vendors and the
proposals provided. In short, the total cost associated with each proposal is as follows:

  Year One Cost  $29,985.15  $17,810.00  $17,230.00  $6,834.00
  Year Two+ Cost  $4,725.00  $6,9000.oo  $17,230.00  $3,435.00

In addition to attending demonstrations provided by the website developers, City Staff explored
City websites created by each firm.
 With a small staff, efficiency has been at the forefront of internal conversations. By better utilizing
technology, specifically, the City’s website, City Staff hope to streamline processes, and provide
better overall customer service and accessibility.

Though Town Web provided the least expensive proposal, the offerings are not robust. In terms
of overall functionality the offerings of QScend, and Revize are not comparable to CivicPlus.

In addition to the website redesign, Staff recommend the integration of CivcPlus’s CivicOptimize
platform. This platform will allow Staff to develop an automated workflow for information or
requests collected from citizens, as well as a progressive web app so the public may efficiently
conduct City business from their smartphones.

The proposal to integrate CivicOptimize is $9,255.50 for the initial set up, and $5,591.25 annually
for year two+ of service.

Through an updated website, integration of push notifications, and development of a user
friendly app, it is estimated City Staff will save hundreds of working hours spent on chasing
paperwork, providing updates on status of citizen requests, and waiting on information.

At this time, the City uses QScend for website development and Grannicus for hosting, posting
and live streaming public meetings. The annual fee for Grannicus, including e-Comments
functionality, is $5,288. The annual fee for QScend is $8,571.

If the City Council authorizes replacement of QScend and Grannicus with CivicPlus platforms
including CivicOptimize, after year two there will be an annual cost savings of $3,543.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Fiscal responsibility, citizen engagement and public transparency.

FISCAL IMPACTS: $50,000 with $25,000 allocation in the midyear budget review for FY 2022-
23- account #10135-5005 and the remaining balance to be budgeted in FY2023-24.

property owner at 215 Beacon, is requesting approval of a Site Plan (companion application) to
allow the remodel of an existing portion of publicly owned property fronting 209 Beacon Street
in the High Density Residential zone. The scope of work includes alterations to
accessory/landscaping structures currently located within the City right of way, which will also
require approval of an Encroachment from City Council. The project is in the Coastal Zone and
is exempt from a Coastal Development Permit (“CDP”) according to Municipal Code section 9-
8.102(b)(2), as well as outside of the 300’ appealable zone. The project is Categorically Exempt
under Section 15301 of the State CEQA Guidelines Existing Facilities.

disqualifies it as a “minor renovation” as defined in the municipal code. The item was brought
before the City of Avalon Planning Commission ata regularly scheduled meeting on March 16,
2022 (PC #2787), approved, and found exempt from CEQA as well as a CDP.

following with an encroachment permit, as the proposal involves work completely within a portion
of the publicly owned street Beacon. Once approved by the Planning Commission, the Council
would be able to make the necessary findings in AMC Section 4-9.106 to authorize the proposed
improvements involved in the site plan review.

  by removing and replacing (much in-kind) the existing informal improvements that exist
  within the City right of way, which is essential in preserving the accessibility of the heavily

Attachment 1: Resolution No. 22-06

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF AVALON,
  CALIFORNIA, GRANTING AND APPROVING A SITE PLAN FOR FRONTAGE
  IMPROVEMENTS WITHIN THE CITY RIGHT OF WAY, AT 215 BEACON STREET; APN 7480
  030-005

  WHEREAS, OIov Nasiek. (“Applicant”) filed an application (“Application”) for the approval
of a Site Plan and companion Encroachment application for frontage improvements associated
with an existing multi-family dwelling located at (“Site”); 215 Beacon Street, Avalon, California,
further described as assessor’s parcel number 7480-030-005, in the High Density Residential
Zone; and

  WHEREAS, This application (Site Plan and Encroachment) for the authorization of
frontage improvements within the City Right of Way was executed in accordance with Avalon
Municipal Code (“AMC”) Section 4-9.103, 9-8.202; and

  WHEREAS, on March 16, 2022 the Planning Commission of the City of Avalon (“Planning
Commission”) considered this item at a regularly scheduled meeting where the Application was
comprehensively reviewed; and

  WHEREAS, pursuant to Title 14, California Code of Regulations, section 15367, the City of
Avalon is the lead agency for purposes of the Project; and

  WHEREAS, the proposed improvements will not have any growth inducing effect and
does not create the need for additional employees, thus the project is allowed by the 2022
Growth Policy; and

  WHEREAS, based on the entire record before the Planning Commission and all written
and oral evidence presented to the Planning Commission, the Planning Commission hereby finds
that the Project is categorically exempt under the following provisions:

Section 15301(e) of the State CEQA Guidelines  —  Existing Facilities.

 (e) Additions to existing structures provided that the addition will not result in an increase of
 more than 50 percent of the floor area of the structures before the addition or 2500 square
 feet, which ever is less; and

  WHEREAS, the project is located in the Coastal Zone, but outside of the 300 feet
appealable seaward area boundary and is exempt from a Coastal Development Permit in
accordance with Municipal Code section 9-8.102(b)(2) ; and

Page 1
   WHEREAS, all other legal prerequisites for the consideration of the Site Plan, Setback
Variance, and have occurred.

  NOW, THEREFORE, the Planning Commission of the City of Avalon does hereby determine
and find as follows:

  Section 1. All Recitals shall be incorporated into this Resolution by reference. Pursuant to
Section AMC 9-8.203, and based on the entire record before the Planning Commission, all written
and oral evidence presented to the Planning Commission, and the findings set forth below, the
Planning Commission approves the Site Plan subject to the conditions set forth in the attached
Exhibit “A”

(a) Every use, development of land and application of development standards shall take place
in compliance with all applicable provisions of this title. The proposed project complies with all
the development standards for the High Density Residential zone and provides additional off-
street parking open to the general public. A variance is not required for the scope of work as
none of the planned improvements contribute to any nonconformance within the front property
setback, and staff has confirmed that the entire project is fully within the public Right of Way,
necessitating a City Council-approved encroachment permit. The design upgrades are calculated
by a licensed Civil Engineer and are intended to have a minimal visual impact on the existing area,
utilizing like-for-like replacement where possible while also stabilizing and reinforcing the hillside.

(b) Every use, development of land and application of development standards shall be
considered on the basis of the suitability of the site for the particular use or development in
tended, and the total development, including the application of prescribed development
standards, shall be so arranged as to avoid traffic congestion, insure the protection of public
health, safety and general welfare, prevent adverse effects on neighboring property and shall
be in general accord with all elements of the General Plan. The project involves an existing
duplex in the High Density Residential zone and a portion of an undeveloped public street. The
proposed changes will mitigate public safety risks by removing and replacing (much in-kind) the
existing informal improvements that exist within the City right of way, which is essential in
preserving the accessibility of the heavily sloped area. The scope of work does not include the
addition of any traffic lanes and will provide for safer, continuous vehicle access as well as off
street public parking, universally benefitting property owners along Beacon.

(c) Every use, development of land, application of development standards shall be considered
on the basis of suitable and functional development design, but is not intended that such
approval be interpreted to require a particular style or type of architecture. Application
materials indicate that the proposed improvements are consistent with the existing character of
this area, and will be reutilizing any original material to be removed during the
stabilization/widening of the Burma Trail.

  Section 2. Based on the entire record before the Planning Commission and all written and
oral evidence presented to the Planning Commission, the Planning Commission hereby finds the

Page2

  /
 nature and extent of the dedications, reservations, impact fees, and other exactions set forth in
Exhibit “A”, if any, are reasonably related to public needs and roughly proportional to the impacts
created by this Site Plan approval.

  Section 3. Pursuant to 9-8.601 of the Code, this approval shall become effective fifteen
(15) days after the receipt by the Applicant of a written notice of action taken unless an appeal
has been made to the City Clerk of Avalon within the said fifteen (15) days.

  Section 4. The Chair of the Planning Commission shall sign this Resolution and the
Secretary of the Planning Commission shall certify the adoption thereof.

  NOW, THEREFORE BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED by the Planning Commission of the City of
Avalon that the Application is hereby approved, subject to the Conditions of Approval in Exhibit
A, and that a copy of this Resolution be delivered to the City Clerk as well as the Applicant.

  PASSED, APPROVED AND ADOPTED this 16th day of March, 2022.

  Chairman Eric Huart

  Conditions of Approval
  215 Beacon Street

  The following conditions are specific to PC Application #2786:

  1.  This project approval shall expire on March 16, 2025 unless a time extension is requested,
  approved, and filed with the Planning Department prior to expiration.

  2.  All access roads, yards and parking areas shall be properly maintained for life of the project.

  3.  The Commission may impose additional conditions as are deemed necessary at the time of
  discussion to protect the public health, safety and general welfare, including any pertinent
  factors affecting the establishment, operation or maintenance of the requested use.

  Site Plan

  4.  Prior to this permit becoming valid, effective or operative, an Encroachment Permit must
  be issued by the City Council in accordance with AMC Section 4-9.105.

  5.  The Encroachment shall not interfere with the public’s use of Beacon Street included in
  the City Right of Way. This intent of this permit shall not authorize the exclusive, private
  use of any of the proposed improvements, including parking spaces.

  The following conditions require additional action by or documentation from, the applicant
  before building permits can be issued:

  The California Department of Fish & Wildlife filing fee shall be submitted as required by
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) statute, Section 21089(b) and Fish and Game Code
  Section 711.4. The fee should be paid within five (5) days of approval of the environmental
  filing at the Los Angeles County Clerk’s Office. Once fees have been paid, the applicant shall
  submit a copy of all documentation to the City of Avalon, verifying the fees have been paid.
  Said permit shall not become valid, vested or operative until the fee has been paid.

  No development, including demolition/construction work, shall commence on the subject
  property until appropriate permits have been applied for and obtained from City of Avalon
  Building  and  Safety  Department.

  If applicable, confirmation is provided by SCE that this project will not require additional fresh
  water.

  Projects resulting in demolition of existing structures or projects exceeding $75,000 in value
  must provide certification of the condition of the sewer lateral before building permits can be
  issued.

Page 5
   Projects involving structures constructed before 1979 and that requires any demolition, must
  be assessed for the presence of asbestos, lead and other hazardous materials which shall be
  handled in accordance with applicable State codes, South Coast Air Quality Management
  District regulations, as well as the Federal National Emissions Standard for Hazardous Air
  Pollutants (NESHAP). Copies of inspection results and shipping manifests (when disposal is
  required) must be provided prior to issuance of a demolition permit or building (major
  renovation) permit.

  Projects requiring excavation and/or grading in a mapped archeologically area defined in the
  Cultural Resources Management Plan for the City, may be required to have a qualified
  archeological monitor onsite during excavation and/or grading.

  Projects requiring obstruction of the public right of way must obtain obstruction permits prior
  to or simultaneous with the issuance of a building permit.

  Projects requiring excavation in the public right of way must obtain excavation permits prior to
  or simultaneous with the issuance of a building permit.

  Projects subject to payment of Long Beach Unified School District fees must provide proof of
  payment or exemption prior to issuance of the building permit.

  The following conditions apply to all projects:

  The project shall be under construction (defined as foundations in and framing in progress)
  within 36 months of this approval or all permits will be null and void.

  Projects located in the floodplain as defined by the FIRM (Flood Insurance Rate Map), must
  provide a base flood elevation certificate for the new or substantially improved structure
  resulting from this application before a building permit can be issued.

  Legal lot status must be verified in compliance with local and state subdivision laws, including
  the Subdivision Map Act (“SMA”) prior to the expiration of this project approval. Should any
  land division violation be determined, the applicant may request a Certificate of Compliance to
  create a buildable parcel.

  If the City discovers that material facts were not disclosed by applicant or that facts provided
  by the applicant were different than represented, the City may impose additional conditions of
  approval to mitigate any adverse impacts. The Planning Commission may revoke or modify the
  use permit in the future if the Commission finds that the use to which the permit allows is
  detrimental to health, safety, comfort, general welfare of the public; constitutes a public
  nuisance; if the permit was obtained or is being used by fraud; and/or if one or more the
  conditions upon which a permit was granted are in noncompliance or have been violated.

Page 6
   The project shall be developed and maintained in strict accordance with the approved plans
  unless written approval is given by the Planning Department.

  This approval does not abridge or supersede the regulatory powers and permit requirements
  of any federal, state, or local agency requirements, which may retain a regulatory or advisory
  function as specified by statute or ordinance. Authorization by the Planning Department does
  not waive the requirement that the project comply with all sections of the Avalon Municipal
  code and all other relevant local/state/federal regulations. The applicant shall obtain and
  maintain permits as may be required from each agency.

  The applicant is responsible for ensuring that all project workers are informed of, understand,
  and agree to abide by the approved plans and project conditions.

  All construction on the project shall be limited to Monday through Saturday, 8am to 7pm. No
  construction shall occur on Sundays.

  All project contractors and sub-contractors must maintain a City of Avalon business licenses in
  compliance with all local, state, and federal laws allowing them to work in the City.

  Non-combustible roofing materials shall be used subject to approval by the Building and Fire
  Departments.

  Approved fire walls shall be constructed as required by the adopted Building Code.

  Fire Suppression system is required if the project is for:
  a) New Structure; or
  b) Rehabilitation, remodeling or reconstruction of twenty five percent (25%) or more of
  the gross square footage of an existing commercial or multiple unit residential building
  or structure; or
  c) Rehabilitation, remodeling or reconstruction of fifty percent (50%) or more of the gross
  square footage of a single unit residential building or structure and the cost of the work
  is more than $10,000.00.
  d) Change in the use of the building or structure. Change in use is defined as ‘those
  alterations which significantly alter the use, increase the number of dwelling units in
  an existing building or result in a building being held open to the public where the
  prior use was for private purposes only. This could include changes from principally
  permitted to conditionally permitted uses, but excludes the conversion of a single
  family residence from transient to non-transient rental or from non-transient to
  transient rental. The requirement shall apply to changes from commercial to
  residential, or residential to commercial, but would not include expansions of existing
  commercial uses, such as the addition of table service at an existing coffee bar or the
  addition of service of liquor at a restaurant.”

Page 7
   e) Work has been done without City permit(s) and City files do not contain information
  to enable us to determine extent of changes to building. In order to avoid an order to
  install a fire sprinkler system, you must provide valid documentation of the structural
  plan as it existed prior to the un-permitted work.

  The site shall be kept in a neat manner at all times and the landscaping shall be continuously
  maintained in a healthy and thriving condition. During construction activities, the applicant
  shall remove daily accumulation of mud and dirt from any roads adjacent to the site; any
  removal of vegetation or construction materials shall be lawfully disposed of.

  Non-potable water must be used for dust control during construction.

  The entire sanitation system shall be connected to the City salt water system.

  The design and construction of all sewers shall be approved by the Department of Public Works,
  including the design and construction of sewer connections and laterals.

  Structural drainage shall be provided by use of roof gutters and downspouts which allow for
  proper drainage away from the foundation of any structure and which do not cause any pooling
  of standing water.

  All plans and specifications must be approved by the City of Avalon Building Department prior
  to construction beginning.

  City staff shall review and approve location, size and noise output of any mechanical devices.

  Any changes mandated by the City of Avalon Building Department that would require an
  amended site plan must be reviewed and approved by the Planning Commission before any
  construction takes place.

  Owner/Applicant must offer to dedicate to the City the following easements measuring at least
  10 feet in width, if applicable:

  •  Public utilities easement
  •  Water line easement
  •  Sewer facilities easement
  •  Landscape easement
  •  Storm drain easement

  Any existing public improvements which are damaged as a result of construction regarding the
  project shall be repaired or replaced to the satisfaction of City staff at the Owner/Applicant’s
  sole cost before a certificate of occupancy can be issued.

Page 8
   Owner/Applicant agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold the City harmless, with counsel
  reasonably acceptable to the City, from costs and expenses, including attorney fees, incurred
  by the City or held to be the liability of the City in connection with the City’s defense of its
  actions in any proceeding brought in any State or Federal court challenging the City’s actions
  with respect to the project. Owner/Applicant understands and acknowledges that the City is
  under no obligation to defend any legal actions challenging the project.

  Any preexisting Municipal Code violations at the property may be required, in City’s sole
  discretion, to be resolved prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy, even if such Code
  violations are unrelated to the project.

  Project must comply with all mitigation measures noted in any related environmental
  assessments performed in connection with this project, prior to receiving a certificate of
  occupancy.

  All conditions of approval must be completed to the satisfaction of the City Planning
  Department prior to occupancy of the project.

  Project applicant must pay the City all statutory fees under the City’s fee ordinance, unless
  otherwise waived by the Director.
